## The Journey So Far
My technical foundation began with a Diploma in Computer Engineering, which established the systems-level thinking I carried into my B.Tech in Artificial Intelligence and Data Science. Early internship experience provided a strong grounding in dataset cleaning, exploratory data analysis, and feature engineering. However, I quickly realized that building impactful data solutions required moving beyond isolated model training.

Driven to bridge the gap between statistical modeling and usable software, I independently upskilled in MLOps, full-stack integration, and Generative AI orchestration. This self-directed focus shifted my trajectory from writing standard analytical scripts to engineering containerized, end-to-end systems. Today, my work focuses on deploying robust applications—from the tracking and versioning of the NYC Taxi Tip Predictor to the interactive dashboards of my E-Commerce Customer Segmentation engine and the NLP integrations powering the TalentFit Shortlister..
:::

## Technical Philosophy & Principles

::: {.grid}

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-4}
<div class="principle-card">
  <div class="principle-icon"><i class="bi bi-box-seam"></i></div>
  <h4>Production-First Mindset</h4>
  <p>A high-accuracy model is useless if it cannot be served reliably. I prioritize containerization with Docker, deterministic environments, and lightweight API endpoints.</p>
</div>
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-4}
<div class="principle-card">
  <div class="principle-icon"><i class="bi bi-graph-up-arrow"></i></div>
  <h4>Business Value Over Complexity</h4>
  <p>The best algorithm is the one that solves the business bottleneck with the lowest maintenance burden. Simple, interpretable baselines always come first.</p>
</div>
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-4}
<div class="principle-card">
  <div class="principle-icon"><i class="bi bi-arrow-repeat"></i></div>
  <h4>Reproducible Workflows</h4>
  <p>Data science requires strict version control. From data versioning with DVC to experiment tracking via MLflow, every step must be auditable and reproducible.</p>
</div>
:::

:::
